intro.text: An old Alethi royal tradition, long neglected but still known among lighteyes, by which the king grants a favour; King Gavilar Kholin revived it.
A favour the King of Alethkar may grant a lighteyes who has done something impressive before him, such as winning a difficult duel.

description.text: Its origins are unknown. Like the Right of Challenge, it had gone largely unused for centuries before Gavilar's day.
If the boon granted touches another of the king's subjects, that person is bound by it as well.

items.text: Gavilar revived the boon to be rid of Yenev, a rebellious highprince. Torol Sadeas fought a showy duel to awe the crowd, and on his victory Gavilar offered him a boon. Sadeas used it to invoke the Right of Challenge, made Yenev duel him to the death and killed him, clearing the way for Aladar to take his place.

House Kholin tried to trap Sadeas the same way. After Adolin won a four-on-one duel, King Elhokar granted him a boon, and he used it to challenge Sadeas. But Kaladin, who had come to his aid in the duel, demanded a boon too, to challenge Amaram. As a darkeyes he was arrested for slander, and in the uproar Sadeas slipped out of his duel.
